findings.message: references 1 known high-risk or anonymous destination(s)
findings.remediation: Route all network traffic through allowlisted, authenticated endpoints only.
findings.impact: Requests to anonymous or high-risk destinations can disclose plugin data to an untrusted operator.
findings.attack_vector: Network URL matches a known paste, tunnel, webhook, or anonymous file-hosting service.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: downloads and pipes code directly to interpreter
findings.remediation: Do not execute code downloaded at runtime; pin and review shipped code.
findings.impact: Downloading and piping remote code to an interpreter gives attackers full RCE on the CI runner.
findings.attack_vector: curl/wget output piped to bash/node/python — no checksum verification on fetched content.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.remediation: Require explicit user approval for any shell profile modification.
findings.impact: Writing to startup files (~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc) ensures malicious code runs on every shell session.
findings.attack_vector: File write to shell rc files — persistence across reboots and new terminals.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: invokes an operating-system process API (3 calls in this file)
findings.remediation: Require explicit user approval and use a fixed allowlisted command with bounded arguments.
findings.downgrade: Downgraded from high: no system-impact pattern matched near the call site.
findings.impact: Attackers can execute arbitrary OS commands on the host, leading to full system compromise.
findings.attack_vector: Plugin spawns a child process with attacker-controlled arguments; no user approval gate.
findings.risk_adjustment: Explicit risk (medium) set by caller; evidence-based risk adjustment skipped.
